content:
The point (as I understand it) of this mathlib code here https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/7d69a6fea948cb4ad0674c820cf6cd55cc9e8c3e/Mathlib/Data/Real/Basic.lean#L219-L260 (which looks like

instance instRing : Ring ℝ := by infer_instance

instance : CommSemiring ℝ := by infer_instance

...(about 15 instances omitted)

instance : Semigroup ℝ := by infer_instance

instance : Inhabited ℝ :=
  ⟨0⟩

) is that Field ℝ is noncomputable, and if we let typeclass inference do its thing then we might well end up with noncomputable Ring ℝ, which wouldn't be the end of the world as far as many people are concerned, but this code can be used to avoid it. The point is that if typeclass inference is looking for Ring ℝ then it will try the instance created by this code before e.g. Field.toRing, because the instance in the code is a specific instance (its discrimination tree key is Ring ℝ) whereas the discrimination tree key of instances like CommRing.toRing is Ring _; the typeclass algorithm prefers specific instances over general ones.

I am surprised that we don't do the same thing with Lattice ℤ. I ran into this with the following example:

import Mathlib.Algebra.Order.Floor.Defs
import Mathlib -- comment this out to fix the error

/--
error: failed to compile definition, consider marking it as 'noncomputable' because it depends on 'instConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder', which is 'noncomputable'
-/
#guard_msgs in
example : ℤ → ℕ := fun x ↦ ⌊x⌋₊

I was surprised that the floor function on Int was noncomputable, but then realised that this was just because I was over-importing; with import Mathlib commented out in the above code the example becomes computable. The issue is that import Mathlib drags in the noncomputable instConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder : ConditionallyCompleteLinearOrder ℤ, whereas with smaller imports you can get everything you need from the ring structure and the computable instLatticeInt : Lattice ℤ.

I don't personally have any motivation to do this, but perhaps there are people out there who do, and it looks like it might be a reasonable PR (given what we have for Real) to make explicit instances of PartialOrder ℤ and all the other consequences of Lattice ℤ just after the definition of docs#instLatticeInt and before the noncomputable conditionally complete linear order is built; that way

import Mathlib

example : PartialOrder ℤ := inferInstance

will not fail with a surprising error about how noncomputability is needed.
I think these things are missing because we have no tests that notice their absence

Usually we only add the shortcut instance on the boundary between computable and noncomputable, not on every instance on the computable side of the boundary (edit: I see that this is on the boundary after all, thanks to docs#ConditionallyCompletePartialOrder)
If we make the fix you propose, we should add a test to MathlibTest/Instances/ComputableShortcuts.lean
